description: Only films with a replacement cost above 20.99 are included. A cost of exactly 20.99 is left out.

a.request: Among films whose replacement cost is more than 20.99, compute for each rating the average of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values). Then take the simple mean of these per-rating averages, ignoring missing ones. If that overall mean exists, list each rating whose average is strictly greater than it, showing the rating, its average, and how far its average is above the overall mean (all unrounded).
a.sql:
WITH rating_avg AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_ratio
  FROM film
  WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99
  GROUP BY rating
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_mean FROM rating_avg
)
SELECT r.rating, r.avg_ratio, r.avg_ratio - o.overall_mean AS diff_above_mean
FROM rating_avg r
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE o.overall_mean IS NOT NULL
  AND r.avg_ratio > o.overall_mean

b.request: For each rating, average `rental_rate / rental_duration` over films with `replacement_cost > 20.99` (excluding NULLs), then take the unweighted mean of those per-rating averages, and list each rating whose average is strictly above that mean, with its average and its unrounded excess over the mean.
b.sql:
WITH per_rating AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_ratio
  FROM film
  WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99
  GROUP BY rating
),
grand AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_avg FROM per_rating
)
SELECT p.rating, p.avg_ratio, p.avg_ratio - g.mean_avg AS excess
FROM per_rating p
CROSS JOIN grand g
WHERE p.avg_ratio > g.mean_avg;
b.raw: For each rating, average `rental_rate / rental_duration` over films with `replacement_cost > 20.99` (excluding NULLs), then take the unweighted mean of those per-rating averages, and list each rating whose average is strictly above that mean, with its average and its unrounded excess over the mean.

c.request: Using 20.99 as the replacement-cost cutoff for films, compute for each rating the average of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` over the qualifying films (ignoring missing values). Then take the simple mean of these per-rating averages, ignoring missing ones. If that overall mean exists, list each rating whose average is strictly greater than it, showing the rating, its average, and how far its average is above the overall mean (all unrounded). Only films with a replacement cost above 20.99 are included. A cost of exactly 20.99 is left out.
c.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 AND rating IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rating), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_mean FROM per_rating) SELECT p.rating, p.avg_ratio, p.avg_ratio - o.overall_mean AS above_mean FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE o.overall_mean IS NOT NULL AND p.avg_ratio > o.overall_mean

d.request: For each rating, compute the average of rental_rate / rental_duration over films with replacement_cost > 20.99 (excluding NULLs), then take the unweighted mean of those per-rating averages (excluding ratings with no value), and list each rating whose average is strictly greater than that mean, with its average and its unrounded difference above the mean.
d.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 AND rating IS NOT NULL GROUP BY rating HAVING AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) IS NOT NULL), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS mean_avg FROM per_rating) SELECT p.rating, p.avg_rate_per_day, p.avg_rate_per_day - o.mean_avg AS diff_from_mean FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_rate_per_day > o.mean_avg ORDER BY p.rating;
